subject: QBR runway: infra commitment asks + unit-econ sensitivity
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: QBR runway: infra commitment asks + unit-econ sensitivity

Team — QBR is in 12 business days. I ran the infra runway model (attached) to translate our product forecasts and OKR throughput targets into concrete infra commitments for the next 6 months. High-level summary and ask: 

- Why now: We need a sign-off on capacity commitment tiers so we can secure Dedicated GPU blocks at current spot/discount levels and finalize the public QBR slides. Pricing windows for the primary cloud partner expire in ~3 weeks.

- Core levers modeled: committed GPUs (A100-equivalent), steady-state utilization (target %), batching (avg in-flight batch size), and KV/prefix cache hit rate. The attached workbook includes three scenarios: 'Conservative' (baseline demand), 'Expected' (central forecast), and 'Aggressive' (higher growth + lower cache hit).

- Key numbers (Expected scenario): 140 A100-e GPUs reserved, steady-state utilization 62%, effective token cost $0.0029/token (model-level blended), batching avg 8, cache hit 48%. This produces an estimated monthly infra run-rate of $1.15M.

- Sensitivity highlights: every +10pp in cache hit reduces monthly spend ~11–13%; doubling average batch size from 4 -> 8 saves ~9% on per-token CPU/GPU contention; however large batching increases tail latency for synchronous routes — tradeoff noted.

Ask: please review the attached model and reply with: 1) preferred commitment tier (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) and 2) approval to proceed with legal/procurement to lock the selected tier. If you want, I can produce a quick sensitivity table across KV hit = [30, 50, 70]% and batch size = [4, 8, 16] — I think that will make the tradeoffs explicit in the QBR.

I attached a one-pager with commitment tiers and a raw workbook (qbr_infra_runway_model_v1.xlsx) + sim charts for batch/cache impact. Planning to publish the QBR infra slide deck by Friday EOD.

Thanks — Aditya
Senior PM, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr_infra_runway_model_v1.xlsx, sim_charts_batch_cache_impact.pdf, commitment_tiers_onepager.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR runway: infra commitment asks + unit-econ sensitivity

Aditya — thanks for the clear framing and the model. Quick read-through comments: 

1) Assumptions: we need the workbook to show per-route avg tokens and sync vs async split. Our OKR (Deliver <50% tail latency for sync embed endpoints) makes batching levers constrained for those routes.

2) Cache assumption: 48% hit in Expected seems aggressive for some customers — can you show a per-workload split (front-door chat vs long-form generation vs embeddings)?

3) Procurement: before we lock a tier, can you include an option where we reserve 60% of the Expected commitment and leave 40% as burstable (short-term credits)? That will reduce upfront cash exposure.

Action: please run the sensitivity grid (KV hit: 30/50/70; Batch sizes: 4/8/16) and add a small table that maps each cell to: monthly $ delta, months-to-payback (against expected cost reduction from batching+cache), and expected tail latency impact for sync routes. If you can get that by EOD tomorrow I can include the chart in the leadership QBR deck.

Also cc'ing Finance in the next update would be good — I want them to eyeball the runway impact.

-Lauren
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR runway: infra commitment asks + unit-econ sensitivity

Lauren — got it. I updated the workbook with the requested sensitivity grid and the per-workload cache assumptions (sheet 'assumptions_by_route'). Summary of the sensitivity headliners (attached updated workbook + charts):

- Cache sensitivity: 30% hit -> Expected run-rate +21% (~$1.39M/mo); 70% hit -> Expected run-rate -17% (~$0.95M/mo).
- Batch sensitivity: moving avg batch 4->8 saves ~9% on GPU cycles; 8->16 saves additional ~6% but increases observed p95 latency for sync routes by ~18–25ms in our sims.
- Hybrid commit option: reserving 60% of Expected (84 GPUs) + 40% burst pool (on-demand credits / short-term capacity) yields ~7% higher monthly run-rate vs full Expected commit but reduces upfront cash outlay by ~38%.

Proposal: sign off on the Hybrid (60% commit) for the QBR narrative, and authorize a 3-month canary on Dedicated for 50% of async traffic to validate effective cache hit and batch behavior in production. If the canary meets the expected hit and latency targets, we convert another 20% to committed capacity at a pre-negotiated tier.

I attached 'qbr_infra_runway_model_v1.xlsx' (updated) and 'sim_charts_batch_cache_impact.pdf' with the sensitivity heatmaps. If that plan sounds reasonable I will start procurement paperwork and attach the finance ask.

-Aditya

Endorse the hybrid + canary approach from infra ops side. A few operational guardrails we should add before procurement: 

- Billing thresholds and automated alerts at 60/80/95% of committed monthly run-rate. Tie to cost page + Slack channel @infra-costs.
- Contract clause request: one quarter notice to scale down commitments by up to 20% in year 1 if workload growth materially underperforms forecast.
- Canary instrumentation: require per-route KV/cold-start traces and a small sampling of raw tokens for quality/regression checks (PII-scrubbed).

If procurement needs a short justification memo I can draft a 1-pager for legal/finance. Loop finance early.

—Vivek
Director, Infra

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: QBR runway: infra commitment asks + unit-econ sensitivity

Alice (Atlas Health procurement) — forwarding our internal QBR request because we intend to present a Hybrid commitment approach to leadership next week. Atlas has existing integrations with our private deployment pilot; Finance asked for an external benchmark on short-term credits vs reserve buys for comparable healthcare customers.

Could you confirm whether Atlas typically prefers: 1) a 60/40 reserve/burst split with an annualized term at a discount, or 2) a smaller reserve + larger committed credit line with quarterly reconciliation? If you can also share any range you have seen for timing (how long procurement takes once contours are agreed), that would be helpful.

Attachments: commitment_tiers_onepager.pdf (internal)

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
